ns2:course.label: Religions of Africa
ns2:course.description: Explores a variety of religious traditions and experiences in sub-Saharan Africa from an anthropological perspective. Local, indigenous traditions are emphasized, but African experiences of Islam and Christianity are also covered. Same as AFST 468 and RLST 468. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. Prerequisite: A 200-level course in cultural anthropology or consent of instructor; or graduate standing.
